about: A recipe, not game data: neutral ids, our own words, and references into the game (the stage actor name, its process, the archive it loads, the fixed parameter word and home angle). The objects themselves load from the player's own game files; tools/story_mods/game_objects.py --game <dir> --list shows which ones the player's game has.

objects.label: Stone block
objects.description: a heavy stone block of the dungeons that Link pushes and pulls, plain or with a statue on top; it is back in its place when the room loads again

transform.why: its collision and its push steps keep the unscaled block

memory.measured: solid heap 12284 bytes (WWHD_MOD_ACTOR_HEAPS=1, US game, 2026-10-21); the archive is in a permanent pack, already in memory

objects.notes: the game's own stone block word (no switch, no save, no path: 0x8100FF00 is the word of 57 of the game's placements) with home angle z 0xFFFF (no path, no second switch); without a switch the block starts at its placement whenever its room loads; variant statue: the game's osiBLK1 word (type 2, 0x8200FF00: the block with a stone statue on top, own heap 15536 bytes)

objects.label: Heavy block
objects.description: a block Link can only push with the Power Bracelets

transform.why: its collision keeps the unscaled shape

memory.measured: own heap 12080 bytes and about 1 KiB more; the archive is in a permanent pack

objects.notes: the game's Power Bracelet block word (type 3, MpwrB): switch 0xFF, no item, home angle z 0xFFFF (no path, no second switch)

objects.label: Rock
objects.description: a small rock Link lifts, carries and throws; it breaks

transform.why: its collision keeps the unscaled shape

memory.measured: own heap 11236-11312 bytes and about 1 KiB more; the archive is the always-loaded one

objects.notes: the game's small rock word (type 0, 0x707FFFFF: no item 0x3F, no switch 0xFF, no item save 0x7F); it breaks when thrown; without a switch it is back when its room loads again

objects.notes: the game's own Ebrock word (Stone2 type 2, 0xF27FFF3F: shadow, no switch, no item) with its home angle z 0x00FF (no break event), as the game places them; a bomb (type 0x20 attack) blows it apart
